annotation.title_clean: Draft Memorandum: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications
annotation.title_en: Draft Memorandum: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President
annotation.summary_en: Draft OMB memorandum implementing Executive Order 13859, directing US federal agencies on regulatory and non-regulatory approaches to private-sector AI applications. It stresses innovation, avoiding precautionary regulation, risk-based cost-benefit assessment, public trust, and reduced barriers, and asks agencies to submit AI regulatory plans.
key_provisions_or_claims: Agencies must avoid regulatory actions that needlessly hamper AI innovation and growth.
Agencies should avoid a precautionary approach and weigh benefits and costs against the systems AI replaces.
Ten principles including public trust, public participation, scientific integrity, risk assessment, fairness and non-discrimination, and transparency.
Agencies should consider non-regulatory approaches and private-sector standards and conformity assessment before new regulation.
Agencies submit plans listing statutory authorities, AI use cases, regulatory barriers, and planned actions.
